messages.author: 01422303d5bd831f
messages.subject: continuity correction?
parts:
Hello friends,

I´m examining a large enough  dataset (34 items, n=1747) to perform factor analysis. During EFA I use the psych package and polychoric correlations, and I get the warning for continuity correction. Now considering that "If there are many 0’s, the results may become unstable, and different corrections lead to heavily different results (see Savalei, 2011)" I have more than 200 cells with zero values so I do not apply such continuity correction.

Now, I want to perform CFA using lavaan. I include the "ordered=c(Q1, Q2...etc)" option so lavaan will calculate polychoric correlations as well. I am wondering whether lavaan applies such correction or not. (I do not get any warning) I´ve checked running 

lavCor(BALLIefa, ordered=c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "Q5", "Q6", "Q7", "Q8", "Q9", "Q10", "Q11", "Q12", "Q13", "Q14", "Q15", "Q16",
          "Q17", "Q18", "Q19", "Q20", "Q21", "Q22", "Q23", "Q24", "Q25", "Q26", "Q27", "Q28", "Q29", "Q30",  "Q31", "Q32", "Q33", "Q34"))

I do not get any warning for empty cells (as I´ve gotten before). Should I conclude that lavaan does not perform the continuity correction? How can I check?

Thanks in advance,


P.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: continuity correction?
parts: Now, I want to perform CFA using lavaan.

You can also perform EFA in lavaan, although it is not yet document because it is still under early development.  See an example in the last post here:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/112
I am wondering whether lavaan applies such correction or not

Are you referring to add 0.5 to empty cells to provide more stable estimation of polychoric correlations?  By default, only for 2x2 tables.  You can turn that off by setting zero.add= c(0, 0), or turn it on for ordinal data too by setting zero.add= c(0.5, 0.5)

How can I check?

lavInspect(fit, "zero.add")
